scope: Physically-corresponded retail pickup placement for the e1-drive power-up slice. Each pickup is placed at its retail arc mapped through the committed measured-arc <-> retail-arc correspondence table, not by a global arc fraction. A pickup whose retail arc has no correspondence segment is unsupported.
placementRule: segment = the arc-correspondence segment of the pickup route whose retail-arc interval contains the pickup retail arc; measuredArc = interpolate(segment.points, retail.arc); sample = nearest measured sample to measuredArc (ties to the earlier sample); appliedLateral = clamp(retail.lateral, -band, +band); x/z = sample.x/z + leftNormal(sample) * appliedLateral; y = sample.groundY. The left normal is (-tz, tx) of the measured polyline.
unsupportedRule: A pickup is unsupported when its route has no correspondence segment or its retail arc falls outside every segment of its route. The reason names the route, the retail arc and the correspondence ranges. No pickup is dropped silently.
lateralRule: Every retail pickup in pickup-routes.json sits on the retail racing line: lateral = width * offset to within 1e-4 m. The applied lateral is still the origin-relative pickup-routes.json lateral, clamped to +/-band, because that is the documented PWR9 convention and the task keeps it. It is a corridor coordinate, not an offset from the racing line, so it is a project placement choice. The physical claim is the along-track arc correspondence; counts.retailWorldError* records how far the placed point is from the retail world position, dominated by that clamp.
layoutIdentityRule: The correspondence is tied to the exact measured layout it was built from. The module rejects a layout whose length, sample count or first/last sample differ, and returns every retail uid as unsupported with a layout-mismatch reason instead of placing on the wrong course.
